chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:

Beware lest Allah sees you while committing His disobedience, and misses you when it is time for your obedience, so that you become one of the losers. And when you are strong, be strong in obeying Allah, and when you are weak, be weak in disobeying Allah.

key_terms.الْخَاسِرِينَ: The losers (those who suffer loss in the Hereafter)

ai.seo_question: How should one balance strength and weakness in obedience and sin according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This maxim from Nahj al-Balagha encapsulates the Shia concept of *Muraqabah* (consciousness of God), urging believers to actively leverage their capacity (*quwwah*) for worship while using their frailty (*da'f*) to resist sin. It reflects the ethical balance where strength is not merely physical power but spiritual readiness, ensuring that one does not become a 'loser' by failing to meet divine expectations during times of ease.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 383. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:

Fear lest Allāh sees you while committing His sins or misses you when it is time to obey Him and as a result thereof you become a loser. Therefore, when you are strong be strong in obeying Allāh and when you are weak be weak in committing sins of Allāh.
